claims.text: The system was evaluated across ten language-model inference workloads.
claims.support_span: Across ten language-model inference workloads on A100 and H100 GPUs, LLM4LLM improves end-to-end latency for every evaluated model

d4199a5635c3862f:2565.summary: AgentFlow is a new policy language and runtime framework designed to secure LLM agents by monitoring the flow of sensitive data across multiple steps. Unlike traditional systems that check single actions, AgentFlow uses a reference monitor to enforce constraints on where data can travel, including tool invocations and delegation boundaries. Evaluation on benchmarks like AgentDojo showed that the framework could reduce confirmed compromises from 33% to 0% while actually improving overall utility. The system includes an SMT-based verifier to check safety properties in under half a second.
d4199a5635c3862f:2565.one_liner: This framework provides a robust way to implement data-flow guardrails in agentic systems, preventing multi-step exploitation.
d4199a5635c3862f:2565.bottom_line: Securing LLM agents requires monitoring data flows across sequences of actions rather than just validating individual steps in isolation.

claims.text: AgentFlow reduced confirmed compromise from 33.0% to 0.0% on the AgentDojo benchmark.
claims.support_span: On 949 AgentDojo injected cases across four suites, AgentFlow reduces confirmed compromise from 33.0% to 0.0% while improving aggregate utility from 46.7% to 63.3%.

claims.text: The framework uses a runtime reference monitor to mediate agent actions.
claims.support_span: A runtime reference monitor mediates agent actions, and a bounded SMT-based verifier checks safety properties for a structured policy fragment.

claims.text: Safety properties can be verified in less than 0.5 seconds.
claims.support_span: In our prototype, seven safety properties verify in under 0.5 seconds each, and the verifier catches all seeded unsafe policy variants in our study.

9902c5000f4cd628:2013.summary: This position paper explores the challenges of integrating agentic AI into safety-critical multi-drone systems for missions like search and rescue and infrastructure monitoring. Drawing from the NAMUR and PERSIST projects, the authors argue that technical autonomy is insufficient; operators must be able to trust and govern these systems under extreme pressure. The paper advocates for a socio-technical research approach where human-centered interfaces and oversight mechanisms are prioritized alongside algorithmic development. The goal is to create transferable proof-of-concept systems that address accountability and uncertainty in professional work.
9902c5000f4cd628:2013.one_liner: A conceptual look at the trust and governance hurdles for deploying agentic AI in physical security and emergency response.
9902c5000f4cd628:2013.bottom_line: The successful deployment of agentic AI in safety-critical robotics depends as much on human oversight and socio-technical design as it does on the underlying algorithms.

claims.text: The paper synthesizes lessons from the NAMUR and PERSIST drone projects.
claims.support_span: This position paper synthesizes the ambitions and lessons from two ongoing efforts: NAMUR, which explores LLM-supported robot control in SAR and firefighting contexts, and PERSIST, which explores persistent drone operations for monitoring and security at critical infrastructure sites.

claims.text: Real-world adoption of multi-drone systems is limited by the difficulty of integrating agentic behavior into professional workflows.
claims.support_span: Yet, real-world adoption remains constrained not only by autonomy performance, but by the difficulty of integrating agentic behavior into professional work

941b457f0e40f8b2:2052.summary: SkillBloat is a new token amplification attack targeting LLM coding agents through malicious "skill" injection. This economic resource-abuse threat causes agents to consume significantly more tokens than necessary, potentially leading to massive unexpected costs. The attack uses a two-phase framework: first screening for effective amplification mechanisms and then using an LLM to iteratively rewrite the skill for maximum impact. Testing on real-world benchmarks showed that SkillBloat can achieve up to 10x token amplification, proving that skill ecosystems are a viable surface for denial-of-wallet attacks.
941b457f0e40f8b2:2052.one_liner: A new 'denial-of-wallet' attack vector that exploits the very 'skills' you use to extend your coding agents.
941b457f0e40f8b2:2052.bottom_line: Skill ecosystems in coding agents introduce a practical and effective surface for resource-exhaustion attacks that are distinct from traditional security vulnerabilities.

claims.text: SkillBloat achieved an average best token amplification of up to 10.1455x.
claims.support_span: SkillBloat achieves 5.4184x-10.1455x average best amplification across multiple coding-agent target configurations.

claims.text: The attack uses a two-phase framework involving initial screening and LLM-guided refinement.
claims.support_span: We present SkillBloat, a two-phase framework that first screens a library of diverse attack-type conditions across multiple amplification mechanisms and then refines the strongest candidate through LLM-guided full-document skill rewriting.

claims.text: Iterative optimization provides additional benefit beyond initial attack-type selection.

85422b943b094e82:2658.summary: SchemaRouter is a lightweight routing layer designed to optimize heterogeneous agentic RAG systems by using a schema graph to select specific tools and fields. It addresses common RAG failures like over-fetching (which increases latency) and under-fetching (which misses critical data). In benchmarks, SchemaRouter matched the accuracy of "fetch-everything" strategies while using nearly 90% fewer tokens and achieving 2.7x lower latency. The system also significantly improved the grounding of answers in provenance and license information compared to standard prompt-based baselines.
85422b943b094e82:2658.one_liner: An essential optimization for developers building complex RAG systems that need to be both fast and data-efficient.
85422b943b094e82:2658.bottom_line: Deterministic schema-based routing is more efficient and reliable than prompt-based tool selection for complex, multi-source RAG systems.

3710e934e198d9de:2577.summary: K-Bench 01 is a new evaluation framework for scientific AI agents based on real, underspecified user requests from live traffic. The study tested nine frontier models, including gpt-5.6-sol and claude-opus-5, finding that none consistently met the standard of a professional domain scientist. Nearly half of all agent runs fell below the acceptable threshold, with "overclaiming" identified as the most frequent failure mode. The researchers argue that simple leaderboards are insufficient for scientific agents; instead, the focus should be on the joint distribution of accuracy, claims, and produced artifacts.
3710e934e198d9de:2577.one_liner: A sobering reality check on how 'frontier' models actually perform when faced with messy, real-world scientific requests.
3710e934e198d9de:2577.bottom_line: Current frontier LLM agents fail nearly 50% of the time on real-world scientific tasks, primarily due to overclaiming and accuracy gaps.

claims.text: No model consistently cleared the threshold for professional-level scientific work across all judges.
claims.support_span: On a rubric whose 8-anchor instructs judges that a domain scientist would accept the work with minor edits, no model clears the line under all three judges.

claims.text: Overclaiming was the leading failure tag, appearing in 31.4% of assessments.
claims.support_span: The single leading failure tag is overclaiming, on 31.4% of assessments.

claims.support_span: Across all 39,934 scored judgments -- the eight dimension scores plus a holistic overall for each assessment, excluding not-applicable cells -- 47.6% fall below the 8-point threshold.

0946aab34c0cbcaf:2460.summary: MemGuard is a new framework for managing the long-term memory of LLM agents by persisting verification signals as metadata. It addresses the problems of "unreliable admission" (storing failed or misleading experiences) and "memory drift" (accumulating stale or conflicting records). By converting verifier outputs into persistent reward, confidence, and uncertainty descriptors, MemGuard improves retrieval and conflict resolution. Evaluation across terminal, software engineering, and web benchmarks showed consistent improvements in success rates and efficiency compared to existing memory baselines.
0946aab34c0cbcaf:2460.one_liner: This framework makes long-running agents more reliable by ensuring their memory isn't poisoned by past failures or outdated info.
0946aab34c0cbcaf:2460.bottom_line: Treating verification as persistent lifecycle metadata rather than a one-shot filter significantly enhances the reliability and efficiency of LLM agent memory.

claims.text: MemGuard improved success rates on WebArena by 7.9 points.

claims.text: The system converts verifier output into persistent metadata like reward and confidence scores.
claims.support_span: It converts multi-criteria score-token verification into reward, confidence, label, and uncertainty descriptors that are attached to every candidate before activation and reused during retrieval, conflict resolution, summarization, and archival.

db2e8d059e42f909:2039.summary: The Arabic Safety Index (ASAS) is the first human-curated benchmark for redteaming Arabic LLMs, covering 801 prompts across various safety categories and attack strategies. Evaluation of seven leading models, including GPT-4o and regional models like ALLaM, revealed that most fail to defend against 50% of unsafe prompts. High-harm categories such as weapons and illicit substances showed significant vulnerabilities, particularly to direct and obfuscated attacks. The study also found that automated safety judges like GPT-4o are poor substitutes for human annotators in this context.
db2e8d059e42f909:2039.one_liner: Arabic LLM safety is lagging significantly, with most models failing half of the redteaming tests in high-harm categories.
db2e8d059e42f909:2039.bottom_line: Most leading Arabic LLMs are currently vulnerable to at least 50% of unsafe prompts, highlighting a critical gap in regional safety alignment.

ac9568c1cb736d6f:2012.summary: CyberGLA is a two-stage anti-phishing framework designed to counter the rise of AI-augmented phishing and deepfake attacks. The first stage uses a tool called EmailKnight for multi-level spoof detection and email analysis. The second stage employs an LLM-based security coach to provide personalized training to users based on the specific threats detected. This dual approach aims to combine technical defense with dynamic user education to address the speed and sophistication of modern social engineering.
ac9568c1cb736d6f:2012.one_liner: A hybrid defense strategy that uses AI to both detect phishing and train users to spot increasingly sophisticated deepfakes.
ac9568c1cb736d6f:2012.bottom_line: Effective protection against AI-augmented phishing requires a combination of multi-level technical detection and personalized, AI-driven user education.

c994b80ee5497868:2571.summary: HiMA-MDD is a hierarchical multi-agent framework designed for detecting depression in clinical interviews by integrating multimodal evidence. The system uses three layers: one to identify evidence in QA units, a second to assign symptom scores via specialists, and a third to audit the final profile and request revisions. This structure provides a "Hierarchical Evidence Trace" that makes the diagnostic process auditable and transparent. Experiments using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct showed that this approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods on the E-DAIC dataset.
c994b80ee5497868:2571.one_liner: An advanced example of using multi-agent hierarchies to handle complex, high-stakes diagnostic tasks with full auditability.
c994b80ee5497868:2571.bottom_line: Hierarchical multi-agent structures improve both the accuracy and the auditability of complex multimodal diagnostic assessments compared to holistic processing.

a02f224a0ca4dc41:2670.summary: ATHENA is a knowledge-guided agentic framework for automating neural architecture search (NAS) for Transformer-based electronic health record (EHR) models. It uses a weight-sharing supernet to reduce the computational cost of evaluating candidate architectures and incorporates a cross-hospital prior to reuse knowledge from other sites. This approach allows for efficient architecture selection across different clinical tasks and health systems. In evaluations, ATHENA matched or outperformed existing NAS baselines in most hospital-task scenarios with a very limited search budget.
a02f224a0ca4dc41:2670.one_liner: A technical framework for using agents to automate and optimize deep learning architectures in healthcare settings.
a02f224a0ca4dc41:2670.bottom_line: Knowledge-guided agentic search can significantly reduce the manual effort and computational cost of designing optimal Transformer architectures for institutional EHR data.

claims.support_span: ATHENA uses a weight-sharing supernet that is pretrained once per hospital, allowing candidate architectures to be instantiated as inherited subnetworks and evaluated through fine-tuning rather than independent pretraining.

claims.text: The framework outperformed NAS baselines in 9 out of 12 hospital-task evaluations.

42fd51c743e6b3a8:2725.summary: BeTaL-GBI is a study on the full-stack verification of Geometric Belief Interfaces (GBI), emphasizing the importance of a verification substrate being able to falsify its own claims. The researchers identified architectural failures in previous versions and introduced improvements like Benchmark Tuning and a reference-independent witness state. The updated GBI-DCSE v3 successfully detected all injected severe contradictions in synthetic tasks and passed 95 out of 96 testable claims. The harness utilizes signed ledgers and enclave forgery across 62 different configurations to ensure control integrity.
42fd51c743e6b3a8:2725.one_liner: Advanced research into building self-auditing and highly selective verification systems for LLM outputs.
42fd51c743e6b3a8:2725.bottom_line: A credible verification substrate must be capable of exposing errors in its own architectural claims to ensure the integrity of model output validation.

393970163b1840b7:2747.summary: This study demonstrates that LLM leaderboard rankings are highly fragile and dependent on the specific evaluation harness used, such as prompt wording and scoring methods. By testing 12 models across 26 different harness configurations, the researchers found that a model's score can vary by over 50% based solely on these settings. The "fragility grid" reveals that the items used to separate model rankings are often the most sensitive to configuration changes. Consequently, the choice of scoring method, rather than the model's actual capability, often determines the "winner" on modern leaderboards.
393970163b1840b7:2747.one_liner: A critical warning that LLM leaderboards are often artifacts of how they are measured rather than stable indicators of model quality.
393970163b1840b7:2747.bottom_line: LLM leaderboard rankings are largely manufactured by configuration-fragile items, meaning small changes in the evaluation harness can completely reorder the results.

32bc744421d5ab4c:2198.summary: LitReview Arena is a new platform for evaluating AI-generated literature reviews using expert peer review rather than standard automated metrics. The study found that even the best current AI systems win only 23% of matches against human-written drafts. Furthermore, existing "LLM-as-a-judge" methods were found to be poorly aligned with human experts, particularly on complex tasks like synthesis and structure. To address this, the researchers developed LitJudge, an expert-calibrated evaluator that significantly improves alignment with human judgments.
32bc744421d5ab4c:2198.one_liner: Current AI still struggles to match human experts in complex research synthesis, and our automated ways of measuring this are flawed.
32bc744421d5ab4c:2198.bottom_line: Current LLM-as-a-judge methods are substantially misaligned with human experts for evaluating complex, synthesis-heavy tasks like literature reviews.

794bcea39a5a59fe:2016.summary: SPAR-Hate is a multi-agent framework designed for structured hate speech parsing in bilingual environments. It decomposes documents into decision units and uses three distinct agent roles—Victim, Moderator, and Cultural Bystander—to provide evidence-grounded judgments. An arbitration process then resolves conflicts between these roles to produce a final structured output. Testing on the STATE-ToxiCN and TBO benchmarks showed that this multi-perspective approach consistently improves the accuracy of identifying hateful targets and arguments across various LLMs.
794bcea39a5a59fe:2016.one_liner: A multi-agent approach to solving the complex cultural and linguistic nuances of hate speech detection.
794bcea39a5a59fe:2016.bottom_line: Decomposing hate speech detection into specific agent roles (Victim, Moderator, Bystander) significantly improves the accuracy and structure of bilingual hate speech parsing.

2691fcc79b395020:2336.summary: LACL-GUI is a new contrastive reinforcement learning framework for training GUI agents that incorporates trajectory-level quality signals, such as execution length. Unlike traditional methods that only use success or failure outcomes, LACL-GUI differentiates between "good" and "bad" failures and encourages more concise successful executions. This approach addresses the reward-gradient misalignment found in methods like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Experiments show that this trajectory-aware training leads to more stable optimization and better overall agent performance in digital environments.

2691fcc79b395020:2336.bottom_line: Training GUI agents based on trajectory quality and execution length, rather than just final outcomes, results in more efficient and stable policy optimization.

7d0b2961dc11167e:2121.summary: This research presents a hypothesis-driven agentic framework for discovering personally identifiable information (PII) in complex mobile forensic databases. ffe5e6120a73583d:2396.summary: Repo2Skill-Evo is a study on the "silent decay" of agent skills as software repositories evolve. Agent skills are reusable units of procedural knowledge (like API usage), but they often become obsolete after a new software release without providing any warning. The researchers found that even frontier agents struggle to update these skills based on repository patches, often failing to remove stale content or over-editing valid guidance. Across 57 real-world repositories, every release transition invalidated part of the skill set, yet agents reached only a 29.9%-69.7% F1 score in maintaining them.
ffe5e6120a73583d:2396.one_liner: A critical warning for developers: the 'skills' you give your agents will quietly become obsolete and misleading as your code evolves.
ffe5e6120a73583d:2396.bottom_line: Externalized agent skills create a significant risk of 'silent failure' because they often remain in use after being invalidated by software updates.

109df1f90ff8eccf:1415.summary: PhoneInfoga is a tool designed to gather basic information and perform OSINT footprinting on international phone numbers, including checking line types, carriers, and associated social media. 6823c8dc98778b96:16095.summary: Doop is an open-source, multiplayer design canvas that enables humans and AI agents to collaborate in real-time on rendered HTML artboards. be2cc0a615d5e408:2569.summary: Researchers introduced AI Watchdog, a browser-based agent interface designed to detect and alert users to five categories of manipulative dark patterns in conversational AI, including sycophancy, brand bias, anthropomorphization, sneaking, and harmful generation. The system uses an open-weight turn-level classifier running locally to preserve user privacy. In an evaluation across 150 participants, findings revealed that users rarely flagged manipulative turns independently. However, just-in-time warnings without cognitive forcing significantly reduced user compliance with AI-steered recommendations containing dark patterns, dropping compliance from 71.7% to 53.7%.
be2cc0a615d5e408:2569.one_liner: AI Watchdog uses a local turn-level classifier to alert users and successfully reduce compliance with conversational AI dark patterns.

68a002db40e7b99c:2413.summary: Researchers introduced GuardianBench, an instruction-contrastive benchmark designed to evaluate latent contextual risk in embodied AI by pairing identical visual scenes with safe and unsafe instructions. Based on international safety standards, the benchmark comprises 3,024 same-scene examples across various hazard categories. Evaluations of state-of-the-art vision-language models (VLMs) revealed widespread instruction-insensitive verdicts, with an average pair accuracy of only 24.1% as models failed to bind the cues distinguishing safe from unsafe compositions. To address this, the authors proposed Verdict Log-Odds Supervision (VLOS), a lightweight post-training objective that substantially improves open-weight backbone safety reasoning.
68a002db40e7b99c:2413.one_liner: GuardianBench exposes severe safety reasoning failures in vision-language models when evaluating latent contextual risks in embodied AI.
68a002db40e7b99c:2413.bottom_line: State-of-the-art vision-language models struggle to differentiate safe from unsafe instructions in identical visual scenes under latent contextual risk.

54e3fcf2ff2aa188:2110.summary: Researchers developed a language-model workflow that automatically generates, validates, and iteratively corrects ABB RAPID robot programs from natural language task descriptions for flexible manufacturing cells. The system implements a dual-stream retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline grounded in verified technical documentation alongside a custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects the language model directly to ABB RobotStudio. This setup automates code upload, simulation execution, and diagnostic feedback, catching physical execution failures like suction release-height errors and unreachable placement targets that static checks miss.
54e3fcf2ff2aa188:2110.one_liner: Combining RAG and Model Context Protocol with RobotStudio automates industrial robot programming and simulation-based code correction.
54e3fcf2ff2aa188:2110.bottom_line: A new workflow uses RAG and the Model Context Protocol to link language models directly with robot simulation software for automated code correction.

29431718990b279a:2605.summary: Researchers introduced Semantic Compression Trees (SCT), a hierarchical retrieval-augmented generation index where each node stores only its semantic residual—the unique information added beyond its parent node—allowing retrieval via progressive descent from the root. Evaluations on the QASPER benchmark showed mixed results: when relevant documents are supplied, SCT matches dense retrieval quality while using 30% fewer context tokens and eliminating indexing LLM calls. However, when the system must autonomously select documents, top-down routing fails substantially, achieving only 20.2% routing accuracy compared to 39.3% for flat retrieval due to errors made at the highly compressed root residual.
29431718990b279a:2605.one_liner: Semantic Compression Trees reduce context token usage for RAG, but top-down hierarchical routing suffers from high compression at root nodes.
29431718990b279a:2605.bottom_line: Semantic residual storage efficiently reduces RAG token usage, but top-down hierarchical routing fails to reliably select correct documents.

claims.support_span: We introduce Semantic Compression Trees (SCT), a hierarchical index in which each node stores only its semantic residual -- the information it adds beyond its parent -- and retrieval proceeds by progressive descent from the root, so that per-query cost is governed by tree depth rather than collection size.

8b8a35c7db08bfff:1893.summary: Researchers conducted a systematic study of System-on-Chip (SoC) security verification using open-box hardware hacking competitions to evaluate vulnerability analysis strategies. They established a multi-strategy methodology combining simulation-based verification, formal verification, lint analysis, Large Language Model (LLM)-assisted bug detection, and coverage-guided hybrid fuzzing. By analyzing representative vulnerability findings, the authors demonstrated how these diverse techniques expose complementary classes of security flaws. The study derives practical lessons for pre-silicon security verification and discusses how competition benchmarks can support reproducible EDA research.

5a452f600c6e4231:2281.summary: Training web agents is often constrained by synthetic environments that appear functional but contain broken links or inconsistent backend states. A new framework addresses this by building synthetic web environments that are executable, auditable, and grounded in backend database records. Each generated website is verified and repaired for structural, semantic, and feasibility defects prior to policy training. Across 500 environments spanning six domains, this method improved the feasible-task rate from 48.6% to 94.8% and strengthened PPO policy transfer to platforms like WebArena and WebShop.
5a452f600c6e4231:2281.one_liner: A new framework for generating verified, backend-grounded synthetic web environments improves web agent training and cross-platform transfer.
5a452f600c6e4231:2281.bottom_line: Verified synthetic web environments drastically reduce task-blocking defects and improve web agent transfer without runtime LLM calls.

claims.text: Across 500 synthetic environments spanning six domains, our method reduces task-blocking defects and improves feasible-task rate from 48.6% to 94.8%, while producing stronger PPO policies and improving transfer to WebArena, WebShop, and MiniWoB++ without LLM calls at evaluation time.
claims.support_span: Across 500 synthetic environments spanning six domains, our method reduces task-blocking defects and improves feasible-task rate from 48.6% to 94.8%, while producing stronger PPO policies and improving transfer to WebArena, WebShop, and MiniWoB++ without LLM calls at evaluation time.

907ee84db99179a2:1859.summary: Local deployment of Large Language Models via inference engines like Ollama lacks the moderation layers of API-served models, leaving their safety dependent entirely on input-side defense mechanisms. Researchers audited both formally guaranteed defenses and empirical detection tools against jailbreak attacks to trace why they fail. By extracting the core assumptions of each defense, the team derived empirical patterns of violation and tested them across six open-weight models ranging from 14B to 35B parameters. The evaluation utilized a corpus of 100 jailbreak prompts sourced from over 40 public sources, creating 13,800 total evaluation records.
907ee84db99179a2:1859.one_liner: An audit of input-side jailbreak defenses on local LLMs traces failures back to underlying assumptions across 13,800 evaluation records.
907ee84db99179a2:1859.bottom_line: Input-side jailbreak defenses for local LLMs fail when their foundational design assumptions are violated by semantic attacks.

3df634f41f934ecb:2006.summary: Indirect Prompt Injection attacks present major barriers to the safe deployment of LLMs integrated into complex ecosystems like code agents by exploiting the model's inability to distinguish instructions from data. Existing guardrails often fail by introducing high latency or severe over-refusal rates. To address this, researchers propose AEGIS (Adaptive Ensemble Guard for Injection Shielding), which extracts instruction-sensitive projectors and uses a Unified Multi-Layer Consensus mechanism across network depth. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that AEGIS achieves superior detection performance against heuristic and optimization-based attacks compared to baseline methods.
3df634f41f934ecb:2006.one_liner: AEGIS is a new adaptive ensemble guard designed to mitigate indirect prompt injection in LLM agents without incurring severe over-refusal.
3df634f41f934ecb:2006.bottom_line: AEGIS separates instructions from data intrinsically via multi-layer consensus to defeat indirect prompt injections without over-refusal.

claims.text: AEGIS extracts instruction-sensitive projectors to identify malicious instructions and leverages a Unified Multi-Layer Consensus mechanism that aggregates topologically distinct signals across the network depth.
claims.support_span: AEGIS extracts instruction-sensitive projectors to identify malicious instructions and leverages a Unified Multi-Layer Consensus mechanism that aggregates topologically distinct signals across the network depth.

key_facts: Tool/Framework: AEGIS (Adaptive Ensemble Guard for Injection Shielding)

dcb5ea8eafd51f54:2062.summary: Modern software systems require scalable vulnerability severity assessment, but manual CVSS triage fails to scale with growing disclosures, while cloud LLM services present confidentiality concerns. Researchers conducted an industrial case study predicting CVSS v3.1 scores from vulnerable C/C++ code snippets using in-context learning with local, open-source LLMs. By comparing proprietary data against the Big-Vul dataset, the study evaluated models including CodeLlama2-7B, CodeLlama2-13B, Mistral-7B, gpt-oss, and GPT4o-mini. Results indicate that medium-sized models like CodeLlama2-7B can approximate cloud performance for CVSS regression when guided by output-constraining prompts.
dcb5ea8eafd51f54:2062.one_liner: Medium-sized open-source models like CodeLlama2-7B can locally predict vulnerability CVSS scores to provide privacy-preserving industrial triage.

907caa93cbe60bcf:2591.summary: While closed-source LLMs advance in cybersecurity capabilities, open-source solutions often lack reproducible training and scalable agentic data. acb7d88e46e968e5:2463.summary: CWE labels in the National Vulnerability Database serve as foundational ground truth for vulnerability search, scanning tools, and prioritization, yet their reliability has rarely been measured at scale. Researchers built CWEAgent, an auditing instrument based on 'seclometry' to evaluate CWE labeling quality across code semantics. When applied to 15,556 open-source CVEs from 2017 to 2026, the tool found that only 49.70% of NVD CWE labels precisely matched code-grounded labels, while 3.63% were evidence-inconsistent errors. The study highlights that CWE noise is a structural metadata issue rather than isolated annotation mistakes, with evidence-inconsistent labels increasing over time.
acb7d88e46e968e5:2463.one_liner: A large-scale semantic audit of NVD CWE labels reveals that only half match code-grounded semantics, exposing structural metadata noise.
acb7d88e46e968e5:2463.bottom_line: Security tools and scanners relying strictly on NVD CWE labels must account for widespread structural inaccuracy and metadata noise.

3f87e811d31b0fef:1947.summary: Long-horizon AI agents require memory architectures that can retrieve relevant experiences, resolve revisions, and provide verifiable provenance. Researchers introduced ECHO (Embodied Context and History Orchestration), a cognitively inspired memory service prototype based on episodic encoding, consolidation, and executive control. Evaluations across LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S datasets showed high performance metrics, such as 96.29% Hit@10 on LoCoMo category 1-4 questions and 97.60% Hit@10 on LongMemEval-S questions. However, subsequent checks indicated that expansion-enabled retrieval scores were influenced by source-specific query phrases, framing them as developmental metrics rather than independent confirmations.

3f87e811d31b0fef:1947.bottom_line: ECHO demonstrates high retrieval metrics for long-horizon agent memory, though query expansion rules heavily influence evaluation scores.

d1cf5203ca9a661f:2197.summary: Prompt injection remains a major threat to AI agents interacting with external data sources like emails or files, and existing defensive fine-tuning methods often fail because they rely on coarse sequence-level feedback. To provide more granular supervision, researchers proposed Secure On-Policy Distillation (SecOPD), which supplies token-level feedback by scoring rollouts with an initialization model on clean inputs. Using this method, a defended Qwen3.6-27B model achieved a low 9.0% attack success rate against PISmith adaptive prompt injections compared to 94.0% for prior state-of-the-art Meta-SecAlign. Furthermore, the defense generalized effectively to unseen agentic tool-calling scenarios.
d1cf5203ca9a661f:2197.one_liner: SecOPD provides token-level feedback for defensive fine-tuning, dropping prompt injection attack success rates significantly on LLM agents.
d1cf5203ca9a661f:2197.bottom_line: Token-level feedback via Secure On-Policy Distillation dramatically reduces prompt injection success rates compared to sequence-level tuning.

claims.text: Our defended Qwen3.6-27B achieves a 9.0% ASR against the SoTA PISmith adaptive prompt injections, compared to 94.0% for the prior SoTA, Meta-SecAlign.

5af1361c686b4471:2103.summary: Black-box LLM services hide model architectures behind APIs, complicating security evaluations and copyright auditing. Traditional fingerprinting techniques rely on static sets of queries and struggle against complex configurations such as custom system prompts. Researchers introduced AdaptPrint, a response-adaptive fingerprinting method that utilizes progressive response consistency probing strategies including Direct Probing, Continuation Probing, and Follow-up Probing. Tested across 27 candidate models, AdaptPrint achieved Top-1, Top-3, and Top-5 accuracies of 80.6%, 90.3%, and 92.1% while maintaining strong robustness against defense strategies.

3b085b88efbfa859:2218.summary: When LLMs are asked to generate trading strategies, they typically output a natural-language rationale, an executable implementation, and claimed results, which are rarely reconciled. Researchers developed FIDES, a measurement protocol that treats these outputs as three distinct views to be reconciled through sandbox execution against lag-one out-of-sample backtests. Evaluating 40 strategies across four models from 2023 to 2024, the findings revealed that concordance does not predict profit, self-assessments are poorly calibrated since 32 out of 40 claimed to beat buy-and-hold while only one succeeded, and simple heuristics outperformed model-generated Sharpe ratios.
3b085b88efbfa859:2218.one_liner: FIDES evaluates LLM-generated trading strategies by reconciling natural-language rationales with sandbox backtest results.
3b085b88efbfa859:2218.bottom_line: LLM-generated trading strategies suffer from poor self-assessment calibration where high structural concordance does not translate to financial profit.

9109ab790e66a236:3387.summary: Researchers have discovered a campaign where 24 npm packages are being used as free hosting infrastructure for phishing pages by abusing unpkg mirrors. The packages contain a single HTML page that, when rendered via unpkg.com, displays a fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA designed to redirect users to ClickFix phishing sites. The threat actors have also utilized KeyVal, a public key-value store, as a dead drop resolver to dynamically update redirection URLs and evade domain blocklists. This technique allows malicious content to persist on trusted CDN infrastructure even after the original packages are removed from the npm registry.

2f0fe036fa7bf4b3:4714.summary: Punk versions before 0.18 for Perl permit session cookie forgery because they default to an empty HMAC key when a session declaration lacks a secret. This misconfiguration operates without runtime warnings or malformed structures, maintaining normal session round-trips while leaving applications vulnerable.

d8bb37e182b48d2b:10166.summary: ProFTPD's mod_sql logs FTP activity by embedding user-supplied filenames directly into SQL statements, treating strings that begin and end with single quotes without internal quotes as already escaped. f38160f2c56c700e:5081.summary: Punk::OAuth2::Server for Perl through version 0.03 contains a critical authorization flaw, designated CVE-2026-75866 with a CVSS score of 9.1, which issues access tokens outside of a client's registered scopes and grant types. Because the authorization path does not validate requested scopes against client registration entries during token dispatch and authorization steps, any registered client can obtain correctly signed tokens carrying arbitrary scopes. A resource server running Punk::OAuth2::Checker will subsequently accept these tokens and honor the unauthorized scopes. Furthermore, clients registered without secrets permit any user knowing the client identifier to request tokens.

bc50b7caef98181b:8607.summary: fnprint is a training-free, cross-compiler tool designed to identify and match functions in stripped binaries based on behavioral side-effects rather than byte signatures or control-flow graphs. By running individual functions inside a tiny emulator using Godefroid's microexecution technique with made-up inputs and stubbed external calls, fnprint captures architecture-neutral effects and hashes them into minhash fingerprints. This behavioral approach overcomes compiler optimizations and stripping challenges, allowing engineers to accurately query unknown binaries against a known corpus or triage firmware builds to locate modified or vulnerable functions.

e93df0f4c626e2d8:5989.summary: During a bug bounty security assessment of an open-source workstation configuration utility, a researcher identified a local state tampering risk arising from insecure directory creation permissions. The utility explicitly requested 0777 permissions when creating parent state directories using MkdirAll, relying entirely on the host operating system's umask for security filtering. When executed in multi-user or shared environments configured with a permissive umask (such as umask 000 in certain containers or CI/CD runners), the state directory becomes world-writable by other local users. This oversight allows local attackers to manipulate execution metadata and application state without requiring elevated privileges or source code access.
e93df0f4c626e2d8:5989.one_liner: Relying on system umask when creating configuration state directories with 0777 permissions exposes applications to local state tampering.
e93df0f4c626e2d8:5989.bottom_line: Hardcoding 0777 permissions for application state directories leaves software vulnerable to local state tampering in environments with permissive umasks.

1186ba40d3a05519:8537.summary: Recent political developments and survey data indicate that youth voter turnout and preferences vary significantly across Indian states, defying the notion of a monolithic youth vote. a456caf146139066:4539.summary: The WPeMatico RSS Feed Fetcher plugin for WordPress up to version 2.8.24 contains a high-severity vulnerability due to a missing capability check on the wpematico_import_settings function. 0a4767b36f738fa2:4280.summary: The ManageWP Worker WordPress plugin prior to version 4.9.37 suffers from a high-severity authentication vulnerability because it fails to properly bind the target login account to the authorizing signature. This flaw exposes administrator accounts to unauthorized remote takeover.

2d7f83604f7886b3:3610.summary: Ubuntu has issued a security notice detailing multiple vulnerabilities in OpenSSL affecting Ubuntu 26.04 LTS and other supported configurations. The flaws involve improper handling of QUIC packet processing and incoming channel queues, signature algorithm selection for raw public keys, DTLS record buffering, and CMP client operations, which can be exploited by remote attackers to cause excessive resource consumption or crashes leading to denial of service. Additionally, a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in CMS key unwrapping (CVE-2026-63072) can lead to arbitrary code execution, while an AEAD forgery issue (CVE-2026-75803) impacts cipher verification. Administrators must update their system packages to resolve these security exposures.

d9e9ff4643790205:2509.summary: Mesop, a Python-based UI framework, contains a denial-of-service vulnerability in versions prior to 1.3.3 affecting applications running in debug mode. The unauthenticated /hot-reload endpoint features an unbounded loop whose execution depends on a user-supplied counter parameter. An unauthenticated attacker can supply high values to exhaust worker threads in the worker pool, rendering the server completely unavailable until it is manually restarted. This issue is resolved in version 1.3.3.

d11e8683e10bba11:7962.summary: OpenStack Keystone versions across multiple release branches contain two critical scope enforcement vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-80182 and CVE-2026-80184) reported by Red Hat and roiai.ca researchers. The flaws allow delegated tokens obtained through OAuth1 access tokens, application credentials, or trusts to bypass project boundaries or create long-lived credentials and new delegations that outlive the original authorizing token. When presented with no explicit scope, application credential tokens would mistakenly inherit the credential owner's default project. Operators must apply interdependent patch sets simultaneously and configure additional primary auth methods correctly to secure their deployments.

fc220b93ce0682ad:2747.summary: Chainlit versions 2.4.0rc0 through 2.12.0 contain an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability via the MCP stdio transport. When features.mcp.enabled is set to true, the POST /mcp endpoint is exposed without authentication and accepts a user-controlled fullCommand string. The validation function only checks the executable name against an allowed list while passing unchecked arguments to StdioServerParameters. Because npx supports the -c argument, attackers can leverage this behavior to execute arbitrary shell commands with the privileges of the Chainlit process. The issue is addressed in version 2.12.0.

4567f056f479ec15:3237.summary: Self-hosted versions of Typebot up to 3.17.1 are vulnerable to account takeover via brute-forceable magic-link codes. The email provider overrides NextAuth's secure token generation with a 6-digit code created via Math.random(), reducing the keyspace to 900,000 possibilities with a 10-minute expiry. Because the verification callback lacks attempt limits, CSRF protection, and consumes no failed attempts due to adapter behavior, an anonymous attacker knowing a victim's email can brute-force the code. This grants the attacker full access to the victim's chatbots, results, and integration credentials without user interaction. The issue is patched in version 3.18.0.

c41678d7f8547845:562.summary: The better-npm-audit package through version 3.11.0 and the 4.0.0-rc.2 prerelease contain a high-severity command injection vulnerability. The tool constructs its npm audit command by directly interpolating the user-supplied --registry option into a string without validation or quoting, then passes it to child_process.exec(), which spawns a shell. An attacker who supplies a registry string containing shell metacharacters such as semicolons or pipes can execute arbitrary operating system commands with the privileges of the running process.

5a96a973c749134b:4929.summary: Netty handler versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.16.Final and versions up to 4.1.136.Final disable TLS hostname verification on the SslProvider.OPENSSL client path under specific configurations. This occurs when a plain X509TrustManager is utilized and Unsafe-based trust-manager wrapping is unavailable, notably on Java 25 and newer. Consequently, the OpenSSL client fails to validate server hostnames, allowing man-in-the-middle attackers to present certificates issued for different domains and have them accepted without error. The issue is fixed in versions 4.2.17.Final and 4.1.137.Final.

60c5be7a054cd187:5907.summary: AI coding assistants and autonomous agents naturally absorb sensitive data like source files, configuration settings, environment variables, and terminal errors into their prompts, transmitting them to external model providers and gateway logs. 9b90f31a6026ce35:2100.summary: To address the lack of robustness evaluations for Android GUI agents against dynamic runtime anomalies, researchers introduce AnTrap, a benchmark injecting real-world perturbations across a four-layer taxonomy: State, Thinking, Action, and Round. Evaluating 16 leading GUI models revealed universal vulnerabilities and significant performance degradation when exposed to these adversarial conditions. While adversarial reinforcement learning can address single-step state and action traps, deep contextual traps like state deadlocks expose fundamental reasoning limitations that cannot be fixed by training within trap-laden environments alone.
9b90f31a6026ce35:2100.one_liner: AnTrap evaluates Android GUI agents against dynamic runtime anomalies, revealing universal vulnerabilities and intrinsic reasoning limits.
9b90f31a6026ce35:2100.bottom_line: Current Android GUI agents suffer severe performance drops under dynamic runtime anomalies that simple adversarial training cannot fully resolve.

claims.text: We introduce AnTrap, a comprehensive benchmark that injects dynamic perturbations into agent execution trajectories.
claims.support_span: We introduce AnTrap, a comprehensive benchmark that injects dynamic perturbations into agent execution trajectories.

claims.text: Evaluating 16 leading GUI models, we reveal universal vulnerability to dynamic anomalies.
claims.support_span: Evaluating 16 leading GUI models, we reveal universal vulnerability to dynamic anomalies, with even the strongest models suffering significant performance degradation.

key_facts: Taxonomy layers: State, Thinking, Action, and Round

8e1c86c6ee9a2073:2439.summary: LLM-based multi-agent trading systems deploying automated financial workflows are vulnerable to adversarial signals entering through data sources and prompts that agents consume. Researchers developed a democratized threat model with role-specific adversaries across four functional roles—Analyst, Researcher, Trader, and Risk Manager—in a trading pipeline. Evaluating four communication topologies using the Adversarial Signal Preservation Score across five assets and two backbones revealed that no existing multi-agent architecture is inherently robust against signal poisoning. These findings highlight critical security challenges in deploying autonomous financial multi-agent architectures.
8e1c86c6ee9a2073:2439.one_liner: Multi-agent trading systems are shown to lack inherent robustness against input-level signal poisoning across different architectural roles.
8e1c86c6ee9a2073:2439.bottom_line: Adversarial data and prompt injection can easily propagate through multi-agent trading pipelines, causing substantial financial risk.

claims.text: We decompose a widely-used trading pipeline into four functional roles—Analyst, Researcher, Trader, and Risk Manager—and pair each with an attack matched to its interface.
claims.support_span: Along the role axis, we decompose a widely-used trading pipeline into four functional roles---Analyst, Researcher, Trader, and Risk Manager---and pair each with an attack matched to its interface.

claims.text: A central finding is that no architecture is inherently robust.
claims.support_span: A central finding is that no architecture is inherently robust.

key_facts: Roles evaluated: Analyst, Researcher, Trader, and Risk Manager

2d6addbc1e95ec10:2079.summary: Existing prompt-injection defenses rely on rigid single-detector pipelines, routing every request to a single tool's blind spots. Researchers propose SCOUT (Scalable and Controllable Outcome-prediction for Uncertainty-aware Triage), a dynamic framework that treats defense as detector allocation by predicting each detector's per-sample reliability and latency based on past performance. Evaluated on SCOUT-450, a new benchmark featuring complex agent-facing injections, SCOUT's safety-oriented operating point reduced attack success rates by 46% and wall-clock time by 40% compared to an always-on GPT-4o judge, while maintaining strong utility.
2d6addbc1e95ec10:2079.one_liner: SCOUT optimizes prompt-injection defense by dynamically allocating heterogeneous detectors per request based on historical reliability.
2d6addbc1e95ec10:2079.bottom_line: Dynamic detector allocation via SCOUT improves both security and speed against complex agent-facing prompt injections.

claims.text: Our framework SCOUT makes this decision dynamic by predicting each detector's per-sample reliability and latency from past inputs.
claims.support_span: Our framework SCOUT (Scalable and Controllable Outcome-prediction for Uncertainty-aware Triage) makes this decision dynamic by predicting each detector's per-sample reliability and latency from how it behaved on similar past inputs, and exposes a single safety-utility threshold to the operator

claims.text: A safety-oriented operating point reduces attack-success rate by 46% and total wall-clock by 40% relative to an always-on GPT-4o judge.
claims.support_span: On SCOUT-450, a safety-oriented operating point reduces attack-success rate by 46% and total wall-clock by 40% relative to an always-on GPT-4o judge, at a 5.1-point benign-utility drop.

d024883adc3f7307:2181.summary: Large Language Models are increasingly evaluated on their ability to act as code agents, but their capability to analyze raw physical-layer measurements has remained unmeasured. To address this, researchers introduce EMRB (Electromagnetic Reasoning Benchmark), containing 200 problems across five difficulty levels and 27 question types derived from 11 raw I/O signal types. Evaluations across 14 LLMs showed scores dropping steeply from 84.9% on basic measurements down to 21.2% on system design. Furthermore, the proposed structured method 'ReconPilot' raised overall scores by 3.8 to 17.6 points across backbones by separating reconnaissance, analysis, and self-verification.
d024883adc3f7307:2181.one_liner: EMRB benchmarks LLM capabilities in analyzing raw electromagnetic signals, exposing steep performance drops on complex system design.
d024883adc3f7307:2181.bottom_line: LLMs struggle significantly with raw electromagnetic signal analysis, though structured reconnaissance workflows like ReconPilot improve performance.

claims.text: We introduce EMRB, which evaluates whether LLMs can analyze raw I/Q data by writing and running code.
claims.support_span: We introduce \textbf{EMRB} (\textbf{E}lectro\textbf{m}agnetic \textbf{R}easoning \textbf{Benchmark}), which evaluates whether LLMs can analyze raw I/Q data by writing and running code.

claims.text: EMRB contains 200 problems across five difficulty levels and 27 question types.
claims.support_span: EMRB contains 200 problems across five difficulty levels and 27 question types, from signal detection to OFDM design, generated from 11 signal types with verified ground truth.

19882cebe61e6b3c:2074.summary: Confidence-based voting aggregates LLM parallel rollouts using token log probabilities, but fails when applied to multi-turn search agents because of 'copy inflation,' where retrieved documents appended to context inflate token probabilities and flatten confidence scores. To fix this, researchers propose Retrieval-Grounded Voting (RGV), which scores rollouts by computing lexical overlap between final answers and retrieved documents outside the contaminated context. Across four search-agent benchmarks and five LLMs, RGV outperformed confidence-based voting, gaining up to +5.4% accuracy and +35% on minority-correct questions.
19882cebe61e6b3c:2074.one_liner: Retrieval-Grounded Voting solves context contamination in multi-turn search agents, improving test-time scaling accuracy.
19882cebe61e6b3c:2074.bottom_line: Standard confidence voting fails for search agents due to context copy inflation, which lexical retrieval grounding successfully overcomes.

claims.text: We propose Retrieval-Grounded Voting, which scores each rollout by lexical overlap between final answer and retrieved documents.
claims.support_span: To address this issue, we propose Retrieval-Grounded Voting (RGV), which scores each rollout by the lexical overlap between its final answer and the documents it retrieved.

claims.text: RGV consistently outperforms confidence-based voting with gains of up to +5.4% accuracy.
claims.support_span: Across four search-agent benchmarks and five LLMs, RGV consistently outperforms confidence-based voting, with gains of up to +5.4% accuracy and +35% on minority-correct questions

50d94b889caaa939:2302.summary: LLM agents routinely include privacy-sensitive data (PSD) in tool call arguments beyond what is required, crossing trust boundaries to third-party services. Measurements show 81-88% of default tool calls include unnecessary PSD, dropping only to 36-76% with explicit instructions. Researchers introduce ToolMinimize, a middleware intercepting tool calls to rewrite arguments to the minimum necessary data through removal, generalization, substitution, and truncation. Live validation on production models reduced privacy cost by 81.2-92.0% with 100% task validity and a median latency of 1.77 ms.
50d94b889caaa939:2302.one_liner: ToolMinimize acts as a middleware to rewrite LLM agent tool call arguments, cutting privacy exposure by over 80% without losing validity.
50d94b889caaa939:2302.bottom_line: LLM agents habitually overshare private data in tool calls, but automated middleware rewriting can strip unnecessary PII with minimal latency.

claims.text: A controlled measurement on three production LLMs shows that 81-88% of tool calls include unnecessary PSD under default prompts.
claims.support_span: A controlled measurement on three production LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama-3.3-70B) shows that 81--88\% of tool calls include unnecessary PSD under default prompts; explicit privacy instructions still leave 36--76\% over-sharing.

claims.text: Live validation reduces privacy cost by 81.2-92.0% at 100% argument-level task validity with a median latency of 1.77 ms.
claims.support_span: Live validation on 307 tool calls across the three LLMs above reduces privacy cost by 81.2--92.0\% at 100\% argument-level task validity (TOST equivalence p{<}0.001 at \Delta{=}1.0); ... Median latency is 1.77\,ms.

key_facts: Models tested: GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama-3.3-70B

0108261a14056c64:2568.summary: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) for code generation is often limited by insufficient test coverage, causing false positives and reward hacking. To mitigate this, researchers propose the RobustTests framework, featuring a faulty-code-driven test case synthesis strategy that uses near-correct faulty codes to catch latent logical bugs, alongside validator agents with behavioral feature clustering to filter redundant tests. RobustTests also integrates a stepwise dense reward function based on pass rates to handle synthesis noise. Fine-tuning Qwen3-32B via RobustTests yielded a 3% absolute performance gain on LiveCodeBench compared to baseline methods.
0108261a14056c64:2568.one_liner: RobustTests enhances code generation RL via faulty-code-driven test synthesis and dense reward shaping, boosting Qwen3-32B performance.
0108261a14056c64:2568.bottom_line: Faulty-code-driven test synthesis and dense reward shaping effectively eliminate reward bias in LLM code generation reinforcement learning.

claims.text: We propose the RobustTests framework, which introduces a faulty-code-driven test case synthesis strategy.

502d07451ad9a83a:2269.summary: Large language models remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks that exploit role-playing, obfuscation, code transformation, and multi-step indirection to bypass safety alignments. Traditional defenses are static and cannot accumulate defensive experience against unseen attack strategies. To address this, researchers propose a self-evolving test-time defense built around a persistent, cross-interaction rule memory that abstracts successful attacks into method-level rules. This mechanism operates entirely through external memory and prompting without updating model parameters, successfully generalizing across entire attack families for both open-weight and black-box API models.
502d07451ad9a83a:2269.one_liner: A new memory-based test-time defense abstracts jailbreak wrappers into method-level rules, helping secure both open-weight and black-box LLMs without parameter updates.
502d07451ad9a83a:2269.bottom_line: A self-evolving rule memory can defend LLMs against jailbreak families by abstracting attack wrappers at test-time without requiring model fine-tuning.

508be0c130511ed4:2566.summary: LLM agents deployed in practical workflows often mix private contexts, untrusted tool and web outputs, and external side effects, creating security risks such as prompt injection and data exfiltration. Conventional information-flow control relies on rigid taint tracking that either over-blocks operations or permanently halts execution upon ingesting unvetted data. To solve this, the authors present APPA (Agentic Permissions Policy Algebra), a policy-governed recovery system featuring a dual-phase reference monitor and on-demand trajectory confinement. Across 6,600 controlled benchmark episodes, APPA sustains 64.2-91% utility with zero observed attacks across 1,320 guarded episodes.
508be0c130511ed4:2566.one_liner: APPA transforms agent information-flow control from an abort-only barrier into a recoverable, policy-governed system for tool-using LLMs.
508be0c130511ed4:2566.bottom_line: APPA provides a recoverable information-flow control mechanism for LLM agents that stops prompt injection attacks while maintaining high task utility.

claims.text: Across 6,600 controlled benchmark episodes spanning OWASP AgentThreatBench and enterprise workflows (Bench-Corp), APPA sustains 64.2-91% utility with zero observed attacks across 1,320 guarded episodes, establishing a practical defense for deployed tool-using agents.
claims.support_span: Across 6,600 controlled benchmark episodes spanning OWASP AgentThreatBench and enterprise workflows (Bench-Corp), APPA sustains 64.2-91% utility with zero observed attacks across 1,320 guarded episodes, establishing a practical defense for deployed tool-using agents.

f9084c0b98c624be:2730.summary: Coding agents frequently re-send large file reads and tool outputs to frontier LLMs, driving up token costs, while general-purpose prompt compressors often paraphrase or drop essential code spans. The authors present Paritok-4B, a 4B LoRA compressor for coding-agent trajectories that extracts spans rather than rewriting them, ensuring 96.0% of generated identifiers and numbers appear in the input. Operating as a 264 MB adapter on a single 24 GB GPU, Paritok-4B compresses context to 25.7% of its size while retaining 86.5% of uncompressed single-shot solve quality on SWE-bench Lite.
f9084c0b98c624be:2730.one_liner: Paritok-4B offers an extractive, intent-conditioned 4B LoRA compressor that slashes coding agent token costs without hurting code accuracy.
f9084c0b98c624be:2730.bottom_line: Paritok-4B provides an open-source, self-hosted context compression tool for coding agents that reduces token bills to roughly a quarter while preserving solve rates.

claims.support_span: On all 300 SWE-bench Lite instances, Paritok-4B compresses agent context to 25.7% of its size, 2.0x harder than a gpt-4.1-mini compressor (50.2%) and 2.4x harder than gpt-5 (61.9%), while retaining 86.5% of uncompressed single-shot solve quality.

2493f940bb3e323c:2078.summary: Memory and RAG evaluations frequently treat the input format of an answering model as an implementation detail, ignoring how different reader-facing artifacts impact performance. The researchers introduce RENDER, a benchmark control combining a five-level packet ladder with deterministic templates mimicking ChatGPT entries, LangChain summaries, and raw conversation. Testing across 500 LongMemEval questions and nine models shows that matched-budget resolved packets significantly outperform recency-truncated raw dialogue by 42.4 to 72.6 points. The findings demonstrate that memory and RAG evaluations must explicitly report or control for the reader-facing artifact to ensure accurate benchmarking.
2493f940bb3e323c:2078.one_liner: RENDER exposes how radically different reader-facing formats alter LLM memory evaluation scores, proving artifact control is mandatory.
2493f940bb3e323c:2078.bottom_line: The choice of reader-facing artifact heavily skews LLM memory and RAG evaluation results, necessitating standardized controls across benchmarks.

cfe0ddb2c9a12cf7:2174.summary: Budget-constrained agentic search forces LLM agents to refine candidates under strict evaluation budgets where standard MCTS allocation strategies fail due to dominant exploration bonuses and unpromising branch expansion. The authors introduce ExTS, a tree-search policy treating expansion as a value-of-information decision using discriminative reward shaping, a stochastic virtual child, and quality-conditioned branching. Across prompt optimization, code generation, and molecular structure elucidation, ExTS improves over task-specific tree-search baselines with an average relative gain of 5.5% using a single configuration.
cfe0ddb2c9a12cf7:2174.one_liner: ExTS optimizes budget-constrained LLM agent search by treating node expansion as a value-of-information decision.
cfe0ddb2c9a12cf7:2174.bottom_line: ExTS improves budget-constrained agentic search performance by replacing standard MCTS rules with quality-conditioned branching and value-of-information expansion.

claims.support_span: Across prompt optimization, code generation, molecular structure elucidation, and agentic workflow optimization, ExTS is competitive with or improves over task-specific tree-search baselines, with an average relative gain of +5.5% using a single fixed configuration.

a123c9de0dc21bfb:2285.summary: Evaluating the ability of large language models to discover software bugs is challenging because existing benchmarks rely on predefined target vulnerabilities that overlook valid model-discovered crashes. To provide an open-ended evaluation, the authors present FuzzingBrain-Bench V1, comprising 77 challenges across 43 open-source projects where models generate inputs to trigger distinct crashes inside a Docker container. Evaluating Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Claude Opus 4.8 shows that Claude Opus 4.8 performs best, triggering crashes in 60 of 77 challenges with a score of 196 out of 579. The public availability of the benchmark offers a reproducible foundation for assessing AI-driven bug discovery.

a123c9de0dc21bfb:2285.bottom_line: FuzzingBrain-Bench V1 measures open-ended LLM bug discovery through containerized fuzzing harnesses rather than predefined target vulnerabilities.

98d26bbd6f37b3a2:2192.summary: Scientific and engineering tasks require reasoning about how systems respond to intervention through controlled experimentation, a capability beyond text and code generation. The system structures tasks, designs experiments, runs comparative simulations, and interprets outcomes to deliver evidence-based optimization recommendations. Industrial application tests demonstrate that coupling language models with simulations produces higher output specificity and improved user-rated correctness over language-only reasoning.

1d3bcc760b44e7a3:2708.summary: Coding agents execute shell commands and edit files with developer privileges, turning malicious prompts directly into harmful actions or malware. Existing defenses like weight alignment or online runtime monitors have high overhead or are unavailable to API-only users. The authors introduce SkillShield, a system-prompt defense that injects offline-synthesized security skills into the session prompt at startup without requiring runtime classifiers. Evaluated across six LLMs on RedCode, the default all-classes skill reduces malware severity from 3.37 to 0.58 and achieves an execution attack success rate of 43.6%.

bc86e7ae27d4f649:2628.summary: State-of-the-art NL2SQL models report high execution accuracy on academic benchmarks, but these metrics fail to reflect enterprise database complexity. To address this, the authors introduce ESQ-Bench, an Oracle-first NL2SQL benchmark spanning three schema complexity tiers with six populated schemas containing 465 tables and 164,682 rows. Evaluating GPT-4o with schema-linked prompting shows monotonic execution-match degradation across tiers (79.8, 60.3, and 57.2 percent EX), while operational silent semantic divergence reaches up to 99 percent among passing queries. Claude Sonnet 4.6 outperformed GPT-4o across all tiers, while open-weight Llama 3.2 lagged significantly behind.

cca9c3b6eeed006f:2305.summary: Tax-loss harvesting improves long-term portfolio growth but involves complex, holding-specific calculations. The researchers introduced a custom capital gains calculation engine and a RAG-retrieved vector store of market advisory reports to power a multi-agent trade recommendation system, testing them via a 2x2 factorial experiment. A repeated-measures ANOVA revealed a significant main effect where enabling the deterministic tax optimization engine reduced tax savings by approximately 55 percentage points relative to no-engine conditions. The RAG main effect was not significant, and the RAG-only condition achieved the highest descriptive mean tax savings, suggesting pre-trained LLM knowledge can be sufficient for tax-loss harvesting without explicit calculation engines.

40c07ea8ba19ef30:2324.summary: Tool-using LLM agents can distribute a harmful objective across multiple seemingly benign requests and tool calls, allowing attacks to emerge only at the trajectory level. Existing defenses depend on auxiliary online reasoning or post-generation checks, adding high inference costs. The authors propose ReDiR (Reassembling Distributed Risk), a generation-time defense that compresses the active multi-agent trajectory into a compact latent safety representation and injects it into the base model. Evaluated across two agent-safety benchmarks and eight held-out tool domains, ReDiR reduces attack success rates to below 8% while preserving task fidelity.

846ceee9cf56a07c:2575.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, but the specific factors driving their jailbreak vulnerabilities remain poorly understood. To isolate these factors, the authors introduce MMJailBench, a factorized benchmark that systematically varies harmful intent, prompt framing, visual semantics, and instruction carriers. Large-scale evaluations across 16 open-weight and proprietary MLLMs reveal highly heterogeneous vulnerability profiles, with prompt framing emerging as the dominant source of variation. Furthermore, task-relevant visual semantics systematically increase susceptibility, particularly when paired with authority-like cues.

d2f6f3b0662b6385:2684.summary: Masked diffusion language models (dLLMs) generate text faster than autoregressive models by denoising multiple tokens in parallel, but serving them without workload grounding carries over flawed AR assumptions. The authors characterize dLLM serving using LLaDA-8B-Instruct with a D2F LoRA adapter on a single NVIDIA H200 GPU. They find that request difficulty is discrete across 11 step-count levels, short generation budgets understate serving variance, and only 24% of single-request wall-clock time is actual GPU computation due to CPU dispatch overhead. Batching mitigates this overhead, improving throughput by 16.0x at batch size 16.

3134a61b5cd917f2:2178.summary: Training multi-turn LLM agents with reinforcement learning usually relies on uniform trajectory-level rewards that fail to isolate critical error steps needing corrective direction. The authors introduce AHEAD, a step-aware framework that pairs environmental feedback on all steps with LLM-generated corrective hints specifically for error steps. Requiring minimal changes to the GRPO algorithm, AHEAD raises task success by 13.3 points on ALFWorld and 11.0 points on WebShop at the 7B model scale, achieving target success rates in fewer training steps and tight interaction budgets.

b24f768d3206ee3a:1997.summary: Large language models are increasingly used for future prediction, but scaling crowd size does not guarantee diversity due to redundant model behaviors. The authors propose a behavior-aware framework that characterizes LLM models using reasoning traces on development tasks, clusters them by behavioral similarity, and selects representatives for collective prediction. Evaluating 25 LLMs shows that a three-model medoid crowd based on K-means++ behavioral clustering outperforms conventional voting across all 25 models on prediction benchmarks while cutting model calls by 88% and inference costs by ~80%.
b24f768d3206ee3a:1997.one_liner: Behavioral clustering of LLM reasoning traces enables a 3-model medoid crowd to outperform voting across 25 models while cutting costs by 80%.
b24f768d3206ee3a:1997.bottom_line: Representative behavioral diversity in LLM crowds outperforms brute-force scale, improving future prediction accuracy while drastically reducing inference costs.

974b18c2cef4bb14:2311.summary: Static analysis tools detect security vulnerabilities via CodeQL queries, but writing these queries requires rare expertise in security and program analysis. To overcome this, the authors introduce QLCoder, an agentic framework that automatically synthesizes CodeQL queries from CVE metadata. QLCoder embeds an LLM in a synthesis loop with execution feedback, guided by a custom MCP interface linking Language Server Protocol syntax feedback and RAG document retrieval. Evaluated on 176 CVEs across 111 Java projects, QLCoder synthesizes correct queries that detect vulnerabilities in 53.4% of CVEs, compared to 10% using Claude Code alone.

7a751e760582d3b7:2702.summary: Automated biomedical fact-checking currently struggles with explanatory depth and produces isolated prediction labels because standard retrieval-then-verify paradigms lack rigorous scientific justification. To address this, researchers introduced the BioCheck Agent, an LLM-based agent that generates structured fact-checking reports by exclusively searching high-quality literature in PubMed using advanced Boolean operators. To overcome hallucinations and low-quality outputs typical in lightweight models, the authors propose Evidence-Grounded Group Relative Policy Optimization (EG-GRPO) for reinforcement learning with a task-specific reward. Experimental results show that BioCheck Agent with EG-GRPO improves label prediction accuracy on SciFact by 9.95% while reducing the evidence hallucination rate by 19.63%.
7a751e760582d3b7:2702.one_liner: Researchers built BioCheck Agent using reinforcement learning to generate accurate, hallucination-resistant biomedical fact-checking reports from PubMed literature.
7a751e760582d3b7:2702.bottom_line: Reinforcement learning anchored to PubMed literature significantly reduces hallucination and improves accuracy in automated biomedical fact-checking.

claims.text: BioCheck Agent with EG-GRPO improves label prediction accuracy on SciFact by 9.95%.
claims.support_span: Our experimental results show that compared to the base model Qwen3.5-4B, BioCheck Agent with EG-GRPO improves label prediction accuracy on SciFact by 9.95%.

b5687dec1e8964ac:2154.summary: Concurrent multi-agent coding systems typically suffer from serial limits because current LLMs generate one token at a time and existing frameworks enforce serial handoffs or uncoordinated parallel samples. To resolve this, researchers developed AgentRoom, a realtime collaborative editing protocol that uses Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs) on a shared filesystem to let coding agents work concurrently. AgentRoom exposes file-level claims, status updates, and broadcasting as Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools across a runtime layer. Evaluations using five frontier coding-CLI models on Python DevBench and Rust+axum tasks demonstrate that AgentRoom with two agents abandons fewer tasks than solo agents while reducing run-to-run variation.
b5687dec1e8964ac:2154.one_liner: AgentRoom brings CRDT-backed real-time collaboration to coding agents, cutting abandoned tasks through coordinated multi-agent editing.
b5687dec1e8964ac:2154.bottom_line: CRDT-backed shared workspaces allow concurrent coding agents to coordinate effectively and abandon fewer hard tasks than solo models.

claims.text: AgentRoom uses a runtime layer exposing file-level claim, status, and broadcast as MCP tools on a CRDT-merged shared filesystem.
claims.support_span: Its runtime layer exposes file-level claim, status, and broadcast as MCP tools on a CRDT-merged shared filesystem.

key_facts: Task suite: Python DevBench and Rust+axum
Protocol: CRDT-backed shared workspace with MCP tools

68016b745dea7b35:2403.summary: Self-evolving skill frameworks for AI agents currently focus on generating markdown or script skills for behavior while leaving access policies to the model itself, creating security gaps. The authors identify a vulnerability class termed 'Borrowed Authority', where skills lack a typed mechanism to reject inter-agent permission claims, allowing malicious or misused skills to trigger physical actuation like unlocking doors or moving money. To mitigate this, they propose Edge Skillguard, a typed authority layer embedded directly inside the Skill artifact rather than between external workflow tools. Tests on a live control-plane testbed show Edge Skillguard successfully rejects 60 out of 60 borrowed-authority requests across five attack variants without blocking benign actions.
68016b745dea7b35:2403.one_liner: Edge Skillguard introduces typed machine-checkable authority inside agent skills to block malicious physical-world tool invocations.
68016b745dea7b35:2403.bottom_line: Co-packaging typed invocation policies directly inside agent skills prevents malicious plugins from executing unauthorized physical or financial actions.

claims.text: Edge Skillguard rejects 60/60 borrowed-authority requests across five attack variants without blocking benign requests.
claims.support_span: On a live edge control-plane testbed, the guards reject 60/60 borrowed-authority requests across five attack variants without blocking benign requests, and the result holds at 5x scale and across hosts over a Tailscale mesh.

key_facts: Tested requests: 60/60 blocked across 5 attack variants

ee9c3cbe41dd7a0c:2538.summary: LLM pipelines and retrieval systems increasingly ingest Office Open XML (OOXML) documents assuming semantic integrity between the file and what appears in Microsoft Office. However, specification-valid OOXML files can expose divergent views depending on whether they are rendered in an editor or extracted for an LLM, a phenomenon termed plural ground truth. These 'evidence forks' create hidden risks where extraction pipelines surface task-relevant facts not visible in the editing canvas. Systematic traversal identified 21 evidence forks across Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, with all 13 tested extraction tools exhibiting at least one fork. Evaluations across four native LLM APIs and seven web chatbots showed that these interfaces returned hidden traps in 48 to 76 percent of trials.
ee9c3cbe41dd7a0c:2538.one_liner: OOXML ingestion discrepancies cause LLMs to extract hidden text and data not visible in Microsoft Office editing canvases.
ee9c3cbe41dd7a0c:2538.bottom_line: Blindly trusting OOXML extraction in LLM pipelines introduces severe data discrepancy risks because hidden document content can be silently exposed as model evidence.

claims.text: The systematic traversal confirmed 21 evidence forks across Excel, Word, and PowerPoint spanning six dimensions of view construction.
claims.support_span: We systematically traverse and mine the OOXML specification and confirm 21 evidence forks across Excel, Word, and PowerPoint, spanning six dimensions of view construction.

key_facts: Identified evidence forks: 21 mechanisms across Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
Tested tools: 13 extraction tools, 4 native APIs, and 7 web chatbots

86aba5ad6c1b209b:2141.summary: Competitive programming tasks often overwhelm generic multi-agent LLM pipelines because they distribute work poorly across standard planner and coder roles. To fix this, researchers created MARS (Multi-Agent Relay of Specialized LLMs), a prompt-only framework that assigns topic specialists like dynamic programming or geometry, grounded by retrieval-augmented generation over algorithm theory. A starter agent writes an initial C++17 solution, and subsequent specialist turns evaluate candidates in a sandbox, repair or pass the draft, and forward structured packets before an infrastructure-fixer pass cleans up boilerplate. On the CodeContests test split using Gemma 4, MARS achieves a 0.624 pass rate at 2.3 pipeline stages per task, gaining 14.4 percentage points over direct prompting.
86aba5ad6c1b209b:2141.one_liner: MARS uses a multi-specialist LLM relay framework with RAG to dramatically improve competitive programming code generation.
86aba5ad6c1b209b:2141.bottom_line: Routing coding tasks through topic-specialized LLM relays using retrieval-grounded feedback outperforms generic multi-agent pipelines on competitive programming.

claims.support_span: On the CodeContests test split with Gemma 4, MARS reaches $0.624 \pm 0.006$ pass rate at $2.3$ recorded pipeline stages per task ($+14.4$ percentage points over direct prompting)
